newsitem.title: CANADA: Bre-X shares hit heavy selling at open.
newsitem.headline: Bre-X shares hit heavy selling at open.

text.p: Shares in Bre-X Minerals Ltd sank in heavy early volume on Monday in trade that dealers said indicated institutions were shedding their positions.
Traders said investors were spooked by a raft of media reports over the past three days that appeared to put the company further in a negative light.

"I think it's the highlights in the press," said one trader. He added that while buy orders for the shares well outpaced sell orders at the open, the volume of overall selling was far higher than buying, indicating that it was the large holders who were dumping the stock.
"The orders to sell are institutional, smart money kind of thing, and the buyers are emotionally charged retail guys," the dealer added.
Bre-X shares fell to 2.65 before recovering slightly to trade down 0.43 at 2.75 with more than four million shares changing hands just more than a half hour into the session.

The gold exploration company has been under siege since tests by partner Freeport-McMoRan Copper & Gold Inc on its Busang gold property indicated the deposit may contain "insignificant" amounts of gold. Bre-X had said Busang could contain up to 71 million ounces of the yellow metal.
Bre-X is facing investigation by securities regulators and has been named in several class action lawsuits filed by shareholders in the United States and Canada.

The shares have traded so actively since they resumed in late March that they have been halted several times for technical reasons or have caused the Toronto Stock Exchange's computer trading system to crash.
Stories in several Canadian newspapers on the weekend brought to light several new aspects of the murky Bre-X saga.
According to media reports, an analysis by an Australian mining consultant for Bre-X last year pointed to abnormalities in gold taken from the property.
And a story in Barron's investment newspaper quoted gold analyst John Doody as saying he believes management has failed to adequately defend its methods and estimates.
"(The selling) has got to be a reaction to the Barron's article," said another trader.
"It's trading as if U.S. people are selling it...Guys are just saying, 'Get me out,'" he added.
